title: Database-Specific Field Types in Domain Model
pattern: Using database driver-specific or ORM-specific structural types to represent basic fields inside core domain entities.
why_bad: It ruins portability and breaks persistence ignorance. If you migrate from PostgreSQL to SQLite or a Document DB, your entire core domain codebase must be re-written due to type system dependencies.
detection: Match fields of structs in non-infrastructure folders that are typed with database-driver specific namespaces (e.g., `diesel::pg`, `postgres::types`, `mongodb::bson`).
counterexample: A dedicated adapter module whose explicit purpose is converting driver types to standard types.
fix:
Use standard platform types or clean abstraction wrappers in the domain layer, and map them to database-specific types at the infrastructure boundary.
```rust
struct Order {
    id: u64,
    created_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, // Standard library type
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 6, p. 209); *The Pragmatic Programmer* (Tip 53, "Delegate to Services").
